359624.title: Faudree–Gyárfás–Schelp star-forest ascending decomposition conjecture
359624.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $\binom{m+1}{2}$ edges. An **ascending subgraph decomposition** is a decomposition $H_1,\dots,H_m$ in which $H_i$ has $i$ edges and is a subgraph of $H_{i+1}$ for each $i$. A **star forest** is a forest whose connected components are stars. **Faudree–Gyárfás–Schelp conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with $\binom{m+1}{2}$ edges has an ascending subgraph decomposition $H_1,\dots,H_m$ in which every $H_i$ is a star forest. The paper establishes the broader ascending decomposition conjecture but leaves open whether the decomposition can always be chosen entirely from star forests.

359624.ordinary_proof_or_precise_gap: The source general ascending decomposition uses star forests AND bipartite components; deleting the latter does not retain an edge partition or its ascending embeddings. Its Lemma 21 cannot simply be restricted: a star forest in K_m has at most m-1 edges, so fewer than m/2 such pieces cannot cover binomial(m,2) edges. This obstruction invalidates the shortcut, not the conjecture. A new compatible star-forest partition for every m remains unpaid. Literal nesting of edge-disjoint sets is a transcription issue; source nesting means isomorphic copies.

360002.title: Zhu et al.'s conjecture on acyclic colouring of cubic planar 3-connected graphs
360002.literal_statement: A **cubic planar 3-connected graph** is a planar graph in which every vertex has degree three and which remains connected after deletion of any two vertices. Let $K_4$ and $Q_3$ denote the graphs named in the source, and let the third exceptional graph be the dual graph of $P_4\boxtimes K_2$ as depicted there. **Zhu et al.'s conjecture.** Every cubic planar 3-connected graph other than $K_4$, $Q_3$, and the dual graph of $P_4\boxtimes K_2$ is 3-acyclic colourable. This conjecture concerns the tractability and structure of 3-acyclic colourability in a restricted graph class; the source marks it as open.

375782.title: Weak Roberson Conjecture on non-isomorphic homomorphism indistinguishability
375782.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a class of graphs, and let $\equiv_{\mathcal{F}}$ denote the relation on graphs defined by equality of homomorphism counts from every graph in $\mathcal{F}$. A graph class is **minor closed** if it contains every minor of each of its graphs, and it is **closed under disjoint unions** if the disjoint union of any two members belongs to the class. **Weak Roberson Conjecture.** Every class of graphs that is minor closed, closed under disjoint unions, and is not the class of all graphs has a homomorphism indistinguishability relation that is not equal to isomorphism. This weaker conjecture would still imply that every proper minor-closed, disjoint-union-closed class fails to distinguish all non-isomorphic graphs by homomorphism counts, and it remains open according to the supplied source context.

366851.title: Polynomial-time homomorphism-embedding CSPs for homogeneous Ramsey structures
366851.literal_statement:
Let $\str M$ be a homogeneous Ramsey structure in a finite relational language. A **homomorphism-embedding** is a map that is a homomorphism and restricts to an embedding on every irreducible substructure; the corresponding homomorphism-embedding constraint satisfaction problem asks whether such a map exists from the finite input structure to the target.

**Homomorphism-embedding CSP conjecture.** There is a homogeneous Ramsey structure $\str H$ in a finite relational language, first-order bi-interpretable with $\str M$, such that the homomorphism-embedding variant of the constraint satisfaction problem of $\str H$ is solvable in polynomial time.

The conjecture formalizes the observation that known Ramsey classes often admit polynomial-time algorithms through completion methods. The source presents it as open.

369639.title: The dominant solvable plabic tangle quasi-cluster conjecture
369639.literal_statement:
Let $(G,\mathbf{D})$ be a **dominant solvable plabic tangle**, where $G$ has $n$ outer boundary vertices and inner disks $D^{(1)},\dots,D^{(\ell)}$, and let $m$-VRCs denote the associated $m$-vector-relation configurations. **Dominant solvable tangle conjecture.** There is a normalization of the vectors in the $m$-VRCs such that geometric promotion

$$
\psi:\operatorname{Gr}_{m,n}\dashrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}_{m,D^{(1)}}\times\cdots\times\operatorname{Gr}_{m,D^{(\ell)}}
$$

sends totally positive elements to totally positive elements, and algebraic promotion

$$
\Psi=\psi^*:\mathbb{C}(\operatorname{Gr}_{m,D^{(1)}})\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb{C}(\operatorname{Gr}_{m,D^{(\ell)}})\to\mathbb{C}(\operatorname{Gr}_{m,n})
$$

is a quasi-cluster homomorphism after freezing some variables on the right-hand side. The paper proves the assertion for several classes, but the general statement remains open.

366160.title: Structural conjecture for 3-connected binary matroids excluding M(K_4) as an induced minor
366160.literal_statement:
Let a binary projective geometry be a projective geometry representable over $GF(2)$, and let a **tipped coning** mean a coning operation that retains its tip, while a **tipless coning** means deleting the tip from a coning. A matroid is **triangle-free** if it has no three-element circuits. Generalized parallel connections across projective geometries, tipped conings, and tipless conings of triangle-free matroids are the operations under consideration.

**Structural conjecture.** The class of $3$-connected binary matroids that do not contain $M(K_4)$ as an induced minor is exactly the class of matroids that can be obtained by starting with binary projective geometries and circuits and applying sequences of the following operations: generalized parallel connections across projective geometries, tipped coning, and tipless coning of triangle-free matroids.

This conjecture aims to characterize all $3$-connected binary matroids excluding $M(K_4)$ as an induced minor. The surrounding results establish closure properties for the relevant class under generalized parallel connections and coning operations, but the stated characterization remains to be proved.

357407.title: The infinite Koebe–Andreev–Thurston theorem for plane cellular decompositions
357407.literal_statement:
Let $G$ and $\hat{G}$ be a pair of simple, 3-connected plane graphs corresponding to a cellular decomposition of $\mathbb{C}$ and its dual. A circle configuration is a configuration of circles whose tangency graph is the associated plane graph; write these configurations as $B$ and $\hat{B}$, and denote their tangency graphs by $G_B$ and $G_{\hat{B}}$. **Infinite Koebe–Andreev–Thurston conjecture.** There exist circle configurations $B$ and $\hat{B}$ such that

$$
G_B \cong G \quad\text{and}\quad G_{\hat{B}} \cong \hat{G},
$$

and these configurations are unique up to similarity. The conjecture would extend the finite Koebe–Andreev–Thurston theorem and known infinite results from triangulations to general cellular decompositions of the plane. The source provides no resolution, so the claim remains open.

371097.title: Chudnovsky–Scott–Seymour's Burling-control conjecture
371097.literal_statement: A graph class is **Burling-controlled** when its chromatic complexity is controlled by the Burling graphs, as defined in the source. An induced subdivision of a graph $F$ is a subdivision appearing as an induced subgraph. **Chudnovsky–Scott–Seymour's Burling-control conjecture.** For every graph $F$, the class of graphs excluding induced subdivisions of $F$ is Burling-controlled. This is proposed as a resuscitated form of Scott's refuted conjecture: Burling's construction is the only known obstruction to Scott's statement, and the conjecture remains open.

362227.title: Scott–Seymour conjecture on induced odd subdivisions
362227.literal_statement:
For a graph $H$, an **odd subdivision** is a subdivision in which every replacing path has an odd number of edges. **Scott–Seymour's conjecture.** For every graph $H$ and integer $t$, the class of all graphs with no subgraph isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$ and no induced odd subdivision of $H$ has bounded chromatic number.

This conjecture connects exclusion of complete bipartite subgraphs with induced-subdivision restrictions. The source presents it as an open conjecture combining several themes of the survey.

374968.title: Friedan's reconstruction conjecture for self-dual vertex operator algebras
374968.literal_statement:
Let $U$ and $V$ be self-dual VOAs of CFT type, and let $\mathcal{Z}_{U,g}$ and $\mathcal{Z}_{V,g}$ denote their genus-$g$ partition functions.

**Reconstruction conjecture.** If

$$
\mathcal{Z}_{U,g}=\mathcal{Z}_{V,g}
$$

for every $g$, then $U$ and $V$ are isomorphic.

This is the VOA analogue of Friedan's proposal that a field theory is determined by its restriction to closed surfaces. The source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

366835.literal_statement: Let ${\cal F}$ be a family of sets. Call ${\cal F}$ hereditary if every subset of every member of ${\cal F}$ also belongs to ${\cal F}$. Call ${\cal F}$ EKR if some element $x$ satisfies $|{\cal F}_x|\geq |{\cal H}|$ for every intersecting subfamily ${\cal H}\subseteq{\cal F}$. **Chvátal's conjecture.** Every hereditary family ${\cal F}$ is EKR. The paper describes this as a longstanding and difficult conjecture, with few papers addressing it since its formulation; it remains open in the supplied text.

366954.title: Gir27ao–Janzer–Janzer linear-color exponent conjecture for ordered paths
366954.literal_statement:
Let $P^<_{k,n}$ be the ordered graph containing all edges of length at most $k$, and let $R_<(P^<_{k,n};q)$ denote the $q$-color ordered Ramsey number. For all positive integers $k,n,q$, there are constants $C>0$ and $D=D(k,q)>0$ such that

$$
R_<(P^<_{k,n};q)\leq Dn^{Cq}.
$$

**Gir27ao–Janzer–Janzer conjecture.** The ordered Ramsey number of $P^<_{k,n}$ in $q$ colors admits the displayed bound with an exponent linear in $q$.

The source contrasts this with the known upper bound $Dn^{Cq\log q}$ and records the conjecture as an open improvement for ordered graphs of bounded bandwidth.

367203.title: Trotignon's string-graph or biclique-induced-minor conjecture
367203.literal_statement: A **hereditary class** is a graph class closed under induced subgraphs. A **string graph** is an intersection graph of curves in the plane, and $K_{\ell,\ell}$ is the complete bipartite graph with $\ell$ vertices in each part. **Trotignon's conjecture.** Every hereditary class of unbounded treewidth contains a subclass of string graphs of unbounded treewidth or a $K_{\ell,\ell}$ induced minor for every $\ell$. The conjecture is refuted in the paper using hereditary classes of unbounded treewidth that contain neither an unbounded-treewidth subclass of string graphs nor arbitrarily large bicliques as induced minors.

368354.title: Gartland–Lokastov induced-minor separator conjecture
368354.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a planar graph. A graph is **$H$-induced-minor-free** if it does not contain $H$ as an induced minor, and a graph admits a $(k,1)$-balanced separator if, for every vertex-weight function, it has a $(k,1)$-centred set that is a balanced separator.

**Gartland–Lokastov's conjecture.** For every planar graph $H$, there exists $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-induced-minor-free graph $G$ admits a $(k,1)$-balanced separator.

This conjecture proposes that excluding a large grid as an induced minor is the only obstruction to balanced separators in hereditary graph classes. It is known for several classes, including $P_t$-free, even-hole-free, and three-path-configuration-free graphs, but remains open in general.

368355.title: Georgakopoulos coarse grid minor conjecture
368355.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a planar graph. A graph is **$H$-induced-minor-free** if it does not contain $H$ as an induced minor, and a graph is $q$-quasi-isometric to a graph of treewidth at most $k$ if such a quasi-isometry exists with parameter $q$.

**Georgakopoulos's coarse grid minor conjecture.** For every planar graph $H$, there exist $k,q\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every $H$-induced-minor-free graph is $q$-quasi-isometric to a graph with treewidth at most $k$.

The conjecture is a coarse analogue of the grid-minor obstruction principle and is described as a major open problem in coarse graph theory. The paper notes that the original formulation uses forbidden fat-minors, which is more general than forbidden induced minors.

370726.title: Modified anti-Ramsey formula conjecture for vertex-disjoint triangles
370726.literal_statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be integers with $n\geq 3k$, let $kC_3$ be the vertex-disjoint union of $k$ triangles, and let $G_1(n,k),\ldots,G_4(n,k)$ be the four explicitly defined edge-colored graphs from the paper, with $c(G)$ denoting the number of colors used by $G$. **Modified anti-Ramsey conjecture.** There exists $n_0$ such that for every $n>n_0$ and every $k$ satisfying $n\geq 3k$,

$$
ar(n,kC_3)=\max_{j\in[4]}c(G_j(n,k)).
$$

This conjecture is motivated by extremal constructions for vertex-disjoint triangles and is proposed after the earlier Wu–Zhang–Li–Xie formula is disproved; the source provides no resolution.

371331.title: Signed Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture
371331.literal_statement:
Let $\widehat{K}_2^- = \widehat{(K_2,-)}$ and let $\widetilde{G}$ denote the signed graph obtained from a graph $G$ by replacing each edge with a digon. A finite set of signed graphs is a **GS set** when its forbidden induced-subgraph class has bounded balanced chromatic number. **Signed Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture.** For every forest $F$ and complete graph $K_t$, the set

$$
\{\widehat{(K_2,-)},\widetilde{K}_t,\widetilde{F}\}
$$

is a GS set.

Balanced coloring extends ordinary proper coloring: $\chi_b(\widetilde{G})=\chi(G)$. Thus this is a direct signed-graph restatement of the classical Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, and it remains open.

371766.title: Brown–Graham–Landman Large Sets Conjecture
371766.literal_statement:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{N}$. A set $S$ is **2-large** if whenever $\mathbb{N}$ is two-colored, there are arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$. It is **large** if whenever $\mathbb{N}$ is finitely colored, there are arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions with common differences in $S$.

**Large Sets Conjecture.** If $S$ is 2-large, then $S$ is large.

Every large set is 2-large, so the conjecture asserts that restricting van der Waerden's theorem to two colors is sufficient to obtain the corresponding result for every finite coloring. Brown, Graham, and Landman formulated this conjecture in the 1990s; the supplied source identifies it as open.
